text: This is envoy. It helps residents find public services and take the next step when something is wrong.
The workspace you are seeing is a practice environment. No municipality or employer is participating.
Anyone can begin as a guest. The assistant, service finder, and feedback entry point are visible without an account.
A useful civic journey starts with a source people can trust.
Here, envoy opens the British Columbia job finder, then moves to nearby public service locations.
The Service BC office record shows its publisher, address, review date, and a link to the official site.
A finder link is a route to the publisher. It is not a claim that an individual vacancy is open or that someone qualifies for a program.
Before visiting, residents should confirm current hours and services with the source agency.
A resident can also describe a service problem in ordinary language, without choosing a form first.
In this production chat, the question is about a broken streetlight in Toronto.
Workers AI responds with a reviewable report proposal. The model does not send the report on its own.
Because a similar practice report already exists, envoy warns about the duplicate and asks whether this is a different issue or a recurrence.
The resident can edit, decline, or deliberately approve the next step.
This feedback form works for guests too. The words here are explicitly marked as a practice report.
The form moves to a review screen and states that the City of Toronto does not receive it.
The acknowledgement is still unchecked in this recording, so this draft is not submitted here.
A separate captured practice report was submitted through envoy and received a private receipt. That receipt appears next, with its access token hidden.
For an emergency, residents must use emergency services. This inbox is not monitored for urgent response.
After an approved practice submission, D1 stores the case as the source of truth.
An outbox sends privacy-safe event metadata to Tiger for time-series analysis. It does not send the resident's message body.
This read-only query was taken on September twenty-sixth at nineteen forty-one UTC.
It showed four delivered feedback events and four events in the daily aggregate. Two were submitted and classified events for the practice report shown earlier.
These are dated query results. A fresh event or dashboard view must be checked before claiming a current count.
A staff workspace needs stronger evidence than a sign-in screen.
Auth0 hosted sign-in and the practice organization are configured, but a live staff role token and scoped case action have not yet passed acceptance.
The intended boundary is an Auth0 grant plus matching organization membership checked by the Worker.
Until that is verified, this scene shows the boundary honestly and does not imitate a staff reply.
envoy combines official source handoffs, a guest assistant, and reviewable practice feedback.
Real places and source links appear alongside clearly labeled fictional intake. No government office receives these practice reports.
Next, we need a participating organization and verified staff access.
